title: Hanuman the Brave Helper
bigQuestion: How can every helper, big or small, make a difference?

story.title: The Little Squirrel
story.kicker: A little squirrel rolls in the sand and shakes it onto a bridge of stones.
paragraphs: Big monkeys carry big stones. Splash! They drop them in the sea. They are building a bridge to Lanka. Rama needs it to reach Sita.
A little squirrel watches. "I want to help too," it thinks. It runs into the water. Then it rolls and rolls in the soft sand on the beach.
The squirrel runs to the bridge. It shakes the sand off. The sand fills the gaps between the stones. It does this again and again.
Rama sees the squirrel. He smiles and gently strokes its back. Many families say this is how squirrels in India got their stripes.
story.think: The squirrel was very small. Was its help important? Why?

lessons.title: A Loyal Friend
lessons.mainIdea: Hanuman is Rama's loyal and brave helper.
reading: Rama and Lakshmana look for Sita. They meet a group of monkey people. They become friends. One of them is *Hanuman*.
Hanuman is very strong. He is also very loyal. Many Hindus honor Hanuman. They see him as a model of loyal help.

words.d: Rama's brave helper who leads the monkey army
always staying true to a friend

look.title: Hanuman at the Temple
look.text: Look at the murti in the temple. A murti is a sacred image. This one is Hanuman. He kneels with his hands together. Families bring flowers to him.
look.prompt: Hanuman's hands are together. What might that show about him?

check.q: Who is Hanuman?
check.why: Hanuman is Rama's loyal, brave helper in the Ramayana.

check.q: What does loyal mean?
choices: Always staying true to a friend
check.why: Loyal means you stay true to a friend.

check.q: How do many Hindus see Hanuman?
choices: As a model of loyal help
check.why: Many Hindus honor Hanuman as a model of loyal help.

lessons.title: The Monkey Army
lessons.mainIdea: Hanuman and the monkey army help Rama look for Sita.
reading: The monkey army wants to help Rama. They go north, south, east and west. They all look for Sita.
Hanuman goes south with his group. They come to the edge of the sea. Lanka is far across the water.

words.d: a big group that works together to protect or help

look.title: Looking Everywhere
look.prompt: How many ways did the groups go?

check.q: What does the monkey army do?
check.why: The monkey army helps Rama search for Sita.

check.q: Which way does Hanuman's group go?
check.why: Hanuman's group goes south to the sea.

check.q: What is between them and Lanka?
check.why: Lanka is across the sea.

lessons.title: The Great Leap
lessons.mainIdea: Hanuman leaps across the sea to find Sita.
reading: How can they cross the sea? Hanuman climbs a mountain. He grows very big. Then he jumps!
He flies over the waves. He lands in Lanka. He looks and looks. At last he finds Sita in a garden.

look.title: Hanuman Finds Sita
look.text: Hanuman finds Sita in a garden of trees. He gives her Rama's ring. Now she knows Rama is coming.
look.cite: Retold from Valmiki's Ramayana, Sundara Kanda (Book 5)
look.prompt: How do you think Sita felt when she saw the ring?

check.q: How does Hanuman cross the sea?
check.why: In the story, Hanuman makes a giant leap across the sea.

check.q: Where does Hanuman find Sita?
check.why: Hanuman finds Sita in a garden in Lanka.

check.q: What does Hanuman give Sita?
check.why: Hanuman gives Sita Rama's ring as a sign.

lessons.title: Good News for Rama
lessons.mainIdea: Hanuman brings Rama good news about Sita.
reading: Hanuman leaps back over the sea. He runs straight to Rama. "I found Sita! She is safe!" he says.
Rama is so happy. He hugs Hanuman. Now they know where Sita is. They make a plan to bring her home.

words.d: something new that you tell others

look.title: A Big Hug
look.text: Look at Rama and Hanuman. Rama hugs Hanuman close. Hanuman smiles. The other monkeys cheer and jump.
look.prompt: How does it feel when someone thanks you for helping?

check.q: What news does Hanuman bring?
check.why: Hanuman tells Rama that he found Sita.

check.q: How does Rama feel?
check.why: Rama is happy and hugs Hanuman.

check.q: What do they do next?
choices: Make a plan to bring Sita home
check.why: They make a plan to bring Sita home.

lessons.title: The Stone Bridge
lessons.mainIdea: Everyone helps build a bridge, even a tiny squirrel.
reading: The monkey army builds a bridge of stones. It goes all the way to Lanka. Big and small, they all help.
Many families tell about a little squirrel too. It carries sand. This squirrel story is a well-loved folk telling. It is not in Valmiki's poem.

words.d: a story families pass on by telling it

look.title: The Squirrel's Stripes
look.text: Look at a squirrel in India. It has three light stripes on its back. Families say the stripes came from Rama's fingers. He thanked the squirrel gently.
look.prompt: Why do you think families love to tell this story?

check.q: What does the army build?
check.why: The monkey army builds a stone bridge to Lanka.

check.q: What does the little squirrel carry?
check.why: In the folk telling, the squirrel carries sand.

check.q: Is the squirrel story in Valmiki's poem?
choices: Yes, it is the first page
No, it is from a TV show only
No, it is a folk telling families share
check.why: The squirrel story is a well-loved folk telling, not part of Valmiki's poem.

lessons.title: Rama and Sita Come Home
lessons.mainIdea: Rama brings Sita home, and people light lamps to welcome them.
reading: Rama and his friends cross the bridge. There is a big battle. Rama wins. Sita is free!
Rama, Sita and Lakshmana go home to Ayodhya. It is night. The people light many lamps to welcome them.

look.title: A City of Lamps
look.text: Look at the city at night. Tiny lamps glow on every step. Lamps glow in every window. People wave and cheer. Rama and Sita are home.
look.prompt: Why do you think the people lit so many lamps?

check.q: Where do Rama and Sita go at the end?
check.why: Rama and Sita go home to Ayodhya.

check.q: What do the people light?
check.why: The people light many lamps to welcome Rama and Sita.

check.q: Which festival do many Hindus link to this homecoming?
check.why: Many Hindus remember Rama and Sita coming home at Diwali, the festival of lights.

lessons.title: Lamps at Diwali
lessons.mainIdea: Many Hindus remember this homecoming at Diwali.
reading: Today many Hindu families light lamps at Diwali. Diwali is the festival of lights. Many remember Rama and Sita coming home.
Families in Illinois light lamps too. They share sweets. They tell the story again. Everyone who helped is remembered.

words.d: the Hindu festival of lights in autumn

look.title: Diwali at Home
look.text: Look at the family by the door. Mom sets out little clay lamps. A boy counts them: one, two, three, all the way to twelve. Grandpa holds a box of sweets.
look.prompt: Why might a family light lamps by the door?

check.q: What is Diwali?
check.why: Diwali is the Hindu festival of lights.

check.q: What do many Hindus remember at Diwali?
check.why: Many Hindus remember Rama and Sita's return at Diwali.

check.q: Do families in Illinois celebrate Diwali?
check.why: Many Hindu families in Illinois celebrate Diwali.

review.why: Hanuman leaps across the sea to find Sita.

review.q: What does the monkey army build?
review.why: The monkey army builds a stone bridge to Lanka.

review.q: How does the little squirrel help?
choices: It carries sand to the bridge
review.why: In the folk telling, the squirrel fills the gaps with sand.

review.q: What do people do when Rama and Sita come home?
review.why: People light lamps to welcome Rama and Sita.

review.q: What is the lesson of the squirrel story?
review.why: The squirrel was small, and Rama thanked it. Every helper counts.
